title: Identify a common-reference density quotient with the Radon-Nikodym derivative
source_anchor: Sinho Chewi, Log-Concave Sampling (2026-08-09), Theorem 8.3.1 proof, printed p. 219 / PDF p. 230: the proof identifies mu_t and nu_t with densities relative to the same reference measure m and writes rho_t = mu_t / nu_t, while the theorem statement writes the dissipation using d mu_t / d nu_t.
target_statement: For a sigma-finite base measure m and ENNReal densities p,q, prove that the canonical Mathlib Radon-Nikodym derivative of m.withDensity p with respect to m.withDensity q equals p/q almost everywhere with respect to m.withDensity q, under explicit AEMeasurable, numerator-finite, denominator-nonzero, and denominator-finite hypotheses. Reuse Mathlib's rnDeriv_withDensity_left/right rather than defining a new RN object.

searched: Samplinglib main: TechnicalLemmas/Measure/RadonNikodym.lean already wraps canonical withDensity/RN reconstruction but has no two-density quotient theorem
Samplinglib main: InformationTheory/RNLogRatio.lean fixes the canonical real RN representative as (mu.rnDeriv nu).toReal
Pinned Mathlib: Measure.rnDeriv_withDensity_left and rnDeriv_withDensity_right give the two one-sided density transformations separately
Pinned Mathlib: Measure.rnDeriv_self supplies the common-base derivative
Samplinglib branches/Frontier Cells: no existing common-reference p/q to rnDeriv bridge found
Libraries/shared-foundations.yml: no currently evidenced Riemannian/Optimisation consumer of this measure-theoretic sampling adapter
shared_floor_audit.notes: The hard measure theory is already Mathlib. This cell is a source-shaped adapter that composes the left/right withDensity RN formulas. The explicit finite/nonzero hypotheses are mathematically important: they prevent ENNReal inverse/toReal totalization from silently identifying an invalid quotient. The first focused attempt found two pinned-Mathlib API mismatches (namespace of withDensity_absolutelyContinuous and use of AEMeasurable.mono_ac rather than mono_measure); both were repaired without adding assumptions or changing the target theorem. The corrected exact theorem head then passed focused compilation, the full ASTIS gate, and the site build.
